summary.text: Laurie Jinkins is a Democratic member of the Washington House of Representatives, representing District 27-Position 1 since 2011, and is on the ballot for re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
She was first elected speaker of the House on January 13, 2020, the first woman and the first lesbian to hold the post.

paragraphs.text: Jinkins earned a bachelor's degree and a master's degree from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1985 and 1987 and a law degree from the Seattle University School of Law in 1990, and completed executive studies at Harvard University's Kennedy School in 2007.
Before her election to the House in 2010, she worked as an assistant attorney general in the Washington Attorney General's office and as an assistant secretary in the state Department of Health.
Her other career experience includes work as director of organizational initiatives and as a senior advisor at the Tacoma-Pierce County Health Department.
In 2009, Jinkins co-chaired the campaign supporting Referendum 71, which voters approved.
In 2020 she succeeded Frank Chopp as speaker, and during the 2023-2024 session she chaired the House Rules Committee.
In the 2026 general election she faces Republican Carole Braaten.
